queuePilingHelp: Consumers pull only {{drain}} msg/s; the rest waits in the queue instead of overloading what is behind it.
emptyHint: Drag services from the left onto the canvas, then connect them by dragging from one node's dot to another.
mobileHint: The Lab works best on a wide screen (desktop).

palette.title: AWS services
palette.hint: Drag onto the canvas, or click to add.
palette.dialogHint: {{count}} services — click one to add it to the canvas.

chaos.hint: Break the system to see if it holds.
chaos.azDownHelp: Single-AZ resources fail; multi-AZ fleets lose half (Auto Scaling recovers).
chaos.spikeHelp: A sudden spike of 10× the normal traffic.
chaos.killHint_one: {{count}} node killed (select a node → Kill node).
chaos.killHint_other: {{count}} nodes killed (select a node → Kill node).
chaos.fails: System is DOWN under this failure

cost.disclaimer: Reference On-Demand prices in {{region}}, as of {{date}}. Excludes tax, free tier, tiered pricing and discounts. For comparing options, not a quote.

inspector.usersHint: User traffic is set in the Scenario tab (deselect all nodes to open it).
inspector.label: Display name

scenario.title: Traffic scenario
scenario.hint: Traffic flows from Users through your diagram. Capacity is checked at peak; cost uses the average.
scenario.readRatioHelp: The rest are writes. Reads go through caches/CDNs; writes always reach the database.
scenario.payloadHelp: Drives data transfer out to the internet.
scenario.tip: Tip: multiply requests/second by 10 and see which node turns red first — that's your bottleneck.

review.hint: Click an item to jump to the node.

challenge.manualSg: Security groups start empty here, like a new one in AWS: nothing can connect until you add inbound rules. Select a node → Network → Add rule.
challenge.failed: Not yet ({{score}}%). Check the red requirements.
challenge.hiddenOptimizations_one: {{count}} optimisation requirement is hidden (cache, queue…). Use a hint to reveal it.
challenge.hiddenOptimizations_other: {{count}} optimisation requirements are hidden (cache, queue…). Use hints to reveal them.
challenge.needsOptimization_one: The core requirements are met, but the system is not optimised yet: {{count}} hidden requirement is still failing. Look at the numbers (latency, cost, peak load) or use a hint.
challenge.needsOptimization_other: The core requirements are met, but the system is not optimised yet: {{count}} hidden requirements are still failing. Look at the numbers (latency, cost, peak load) or use a hint.

help.internet: Outside AWS: your users on the internet.
help.edge: Runs at AWS edge locations worldwide, outside your VPC.
help.public: Inside your VPC, in a public subnet: has a route to the Internet Gateway and can get a public IP.
help.private: Inside your VPC, in a private subnet: no inbound route from the internet. Outbound goes through NAT or a VPC Endpoint.
help.managed: Regional AWS-managed service, outside your VPC. Reached over the AWS network (or a VPC Endpoint).

subnet.label: Subnet
subnet.help: Where this resource runs inside the VPC. Try moving it and watch the Review tab.

networkViewHelp: Show the VPC, public and private subnets behind the diagram

net.title: Network
net.sgHelp: Inbound rules: who may open a connection to this port. Security groups work at the TCP level: "HTTP" is just a name for TCP port 80. Replies are always allowed back (stateful).
net.noRules: No inbound rules: nothing can connect to it.
net.resetRulesHelp: Go back to the default rules
net.vpcHint: Address ranges of your VPC and its two subnets. Each resource in a subnet takes a private IP from its range.
net.rtHint: Add a NAT Gateway or VPC Endpoint to the canvas and its route appears here. Connections from the private subnet to services outside the VPC use these routes.
